Two moles of an ideal gas undergo a reversible isothermal expansion at $300 \mathrm{~K}$, starting from an initial volume of $5 \mathrm{~L}$. If the total heat absorbed by the gas during this process is $3.436 \mathrm{~kJ}$, what is the final volume of the gas?

Given: $R = 8.3 \mathrm{~J \cdot K^{-1} \cdot mol^{-1}}$ and $\ln 2 = 0.69$.
questions.question:
Two moles of an ideal gas undergo a reversible isothermal expansion at $300 \mathrm{~K}$, starting from an initial volume of $5 \mathrm{~L}$. If the total heat absorbed by the gas during this process is $3.436 \mathrm{~kJ}$, what is the final volume of the gas?

Given: $R = 8.3 \mathrm{~J \cdot K^{-1} \cdot mol^{-1}}$ and $\ln 2 = 0.69$.
questions.solution:
For an isothermal process involving an ideal gas, the change in internal energy is zero ($\Delta U = 0$).

According to the First Law of Thermodynamics:
$\Delta U = q + w$
$0 = q + w \Rightarrow w = -q$

Given that the heat absorbed $q = +3.436 \mathrm{~kJ} = +3436 \mathrm{~J}$, the work done by the gas is:
$w = -3436 \mathrm{~J}$

The work done in a reversible isothermal expansion is given by:
$w = -nRT \ln\left(\dfrac{V_f}{V_i}\right)$

Substitute the given values:
$-3436 = -2 \times 8.3 \times 300 \times \ln\left(\dfrac{V_f}{5}\right)$
$-3436 = -4980 \ln\left(\dfrac{V_f}{5}\right)$
$\ln\left(\dfrac{V_f}{5}\right) = \dfrac{3436}{4980} \approx 0.69$

Since $\ln 2 = 0.69$, we have:
$\ln\left(\dfrac{V_f}{5}\right) = \ln 2$
$\dfrac{V_f}{5} = 2 \Rightarrow V_f = 10 \mathrm{~L}$

Answer: $10 \mathrm{~L}$

(Given: $2.303 \times R \times 300 = 5744\text{ J mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
For an isothermal reversible process, the work done is given by:
$W = 2.303 nRT \log\left(\dfrac{P_2}{P_1}\right)$

Since work is done on the gas during compression, $W = +11488\text{ J}$.

Substituting the given values:
$11488 = 2 \times (2.303 \times R \times 300) \times \log\left(\dfrac{P_2}{1}\right)$

$11488 = 2 \times 5744 \times \log(P_2)$

$11488 = 11488 \times \log(P_2)$

$\log(P_2) = 1$

$P_2 = 10^1 = 10\text{ bar}$

Answer: $10$

Species$\Delta H_f^{\circ} \text{ (kJ mol}^{-1})$$S_m^{\circ} \text{ (J K}^{-1} \text{ mol}^{-1})$
$A(g)$$-200$$100$
$B(g)$$-150$$120$
$C(g)$$-10$$80$


The standard free energy change ($\Delta G^{\circ}$) for the reaction in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ is ______.
questions.solution:
First, calculate the standard enthalpy of reaction ($\Delta H^{\circ}_{rxn}$):
$\Delta H^{\circ}_{rxn} = \sum \Delta H_f^{\circ}(\text{products}) - \sum \Delta H_f^{\circ}(\text{reactants})$
$\Delta H^{\circ}_{rxn} = [\Delta H_f^{\circ}(B) + \Delta H_f^{\circ}(C)] - \Delta H_f^{\circ}(A)$
$\Delta H^{\circ}_{rxn} = [(-150) + (-10)] - (-200)$
$\Delta H^{\circ}_{rxn} = -160 + 200 = 40 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Next, calculate the standard entropy of reaction ($\Delta S^{\circ}_{rxn}$):
$\Delta S^{\circ}_{rxn} = \sum S_m^{\circ}(\text{products}) - \sum S_m^{\circ}(\text{reactants})$
$\Delta S^{\circ}_{rxn} = [S_m^{\circ}(B) + S_m^{\circ}(C)] - S_m^{\circ}(A)$
$\Delta S^{\circ}_{rxn} = [120 + 80] - 100$
$\Delta S^{\circ}_{rxn} = 200 - 100 = 100 \text{ J K}^{-1} \text{ mol}^{-1}$

Convert $\Delta S^{\circ}_{rxn}$ to $\text{kJ K}^{-1} \text{ mol}^{-1}$ to match the units of $\Delta H^{\circ}_{rxn}$:
$\Delta S^{\circ}_{rxn} = 0.1 \text{ kJ K}^{-1} \text{ mol}^{-1}$

Now, apply the Gibbs free energy equation:
$\Delta G^{\circ} = \Delta H^{\circ}_{rxn} - T\Delta S^{\circ}_{rxn}$
$\Delta G^{\circ} = 40 - (300 \times 0.1)$
$\Delta G^{\circ} = 40 - 30 = 10 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Answer: $10$

The magnitude of the total heat released when $29 \text{ g}$ of butane is completely combusted is ________ $\text{kJ}$.
(Given molar mass of $\text{C} = 12 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$, $\text{H} = 1 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$)

The magnitude of the total heat released when $29 \text{ g}$ of butane is completely combusted is ________ $\text{kJ}$.
(Given molar mass of $\text{C} = 12 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$, $\text{H} = 1 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$)

The standard enthalpy of combustion for $1 \text{ mole}$ of butane is:
$\Delta H^\circ_{\text{c}} = [4\Delta H^\circ_{f}(\text{CO}_2\text{, g}) + 5\Delta H^\circ_{f}(\text{H}_2\text{O, l})] - [\Delta H^\circ_{f}(\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{, g}) + \dfrac{13}{2}\Delta H^\circ_{f}(\text{O}_2\text{, g})]$

Since $\Delta H^\circ_{f}(\text{O}_2\text{, g}) = 0$:
$\Delta H^\circ_{\text{c}} = [4(-393) + 5(-285)] - [-125]$
$\Delta H^\circ_{\text{c}} = [-1572 - 1425] + 125$
$\Delta H^\circ_{\text{c}} = -2997 + 125 = -2872 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Molar mass of butane ($\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}$) $= 4(12) + 10(1) = 58 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$
Number of moles in $29 \text{ g}$ of butane $= \dfrac{29}{58} = 0.5 \text{ mol}$

Total heat released $= 0.5 \times 2872 = 1436 \text{ kJ}$.

Answer: $1436$

(Given: $R = \dfrac{25}{3} \text{ J K}^{-1} \text{ mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:

$\text{C}_{10}\text{H}_8(\text{s}) + 12\text{O}_2(\text{g}) \rightarrow 10\text{CO}_2(\text{g}) + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l})$

The change in the number of moles of gaseous species is:
$\Delta n_g = n_{\text{gaseous products}} - n_{\text{gaseous reactants}} = 10 - 12 = -2$

The relationship between enthalpy change ($\Delta H$) and internal energy change ($\Delta U$) is:
$\Delta H = \Delta U + \Delta n_g RT$

Rearranging to find the internal energy change (which corresponds to the heat measured in a bomb calorimeter at constant volume):
$\Delta U = \Delta H - \Delta n_g RT$

Substituting the given values:
$\Delta U = -5160 - \left(-2 \times \dfrac{25}{3} \times 300 \times 10^{-3}\right)$
$\Delta U = -5160 - (-5) = -5155 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

The magnitude of the heat released is $5155 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

Answer: $5155$

questions.question:
An ideal gas undergoes an isobaric expansion where it performs $830 \text{ J}$ of work. If the molar heat capacity of the gas at constant volume is $20.75 \text{ J K}^{-1} \text{ mol}^{-1}$, the total heat absorbed by the gas during this process is ________ $\text{J}$.

(Given: $R = 8.3 \text{ J K}^{-1} \text{ mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
The work done by an ideal gas during an isobaric process is:
$W = n R \Delta T$
$\Rightarrow n \Delta T = \dfrac{W}{R} = \dfrac{830}{8.3} = 100 \text{ mol K}$

The change in internal energy of the gas is:
$\Delta U = n C_{v,m} \Delta T$
$\Rightarrow \Delta U = C_{v,m} \times (n \Delta T) = 20.75 \times 100 = 2075 \text{ J}$

According to the first law of thermodynamics, the total heat absorbed $q$ is:
$q = \Delta U + W$
$\Rightarrow q = 2075 + 830 = 2905 \text{ J}$

Alternatively, using molar heat capacity at constant pressure:
$C_{p,m} = C_{v,m} + R = 20.75 + 8.3 = 29.05 \text{ J K}^{-1} \text{ mol}^{-1}$
$q = n C_{p,m} \Delta T = 29.05 \times 100 = 2905 \text{ J}$

Answer: $2905$

questions.question:
When $1.4 \text{ g}$ of ethene gas, $\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_4(\mathrm{g})$, is completely burned in a bomb calorimeter, the temperature of the calorimeter increases by $5 \text{ K}$. The heat capacity of the calorimeter is $14 \text{ kJ K}^{-1}$.

Given:
Standard enthalpy of formation of $\mathrm{CO}_2(\mathrm{g}) = -394 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
Standard enthalpy of formation of $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l}) = -286 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
Assume $RT = 2.5 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ and molar mass of $\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_4 = 28 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$.

The standard enthalpy of formation of $\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_4(\mathrm{g})$ is _______ $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$.
questions.solution:
First, calculate the number of moles of ethene burned:
$n = \dfrac{1.4}{28} = 0.05 \text{ mol}$

The heat released at constant volume (which corresponds to $\Delta \mathrm{U}$) is:
$q = C \Delta T = 14 \times 5 = 70 \text{ kJ}$
Since heat is released, $\Delta \mathrm{U}_c$ for $0.05 \text{ mol}$ is $-70 \text{ kJ}$.
For $1 \text{ mol}$ of ethene, $\Delta \mathrm{U}_c = \dfrac{-70}{0.05} = -1400 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

The balanced combustion equation for ethene is:
$\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_4(\mathrm{g}) + 3\mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightarrow 2\mathrm{CO}_2(\mathrm{g}) + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l})$

Calculate the change in gaseous moles ($\Delta n_g$):
$\Delta n_g = n_p(\text{gas}) - n_r(\text{gas}) = 2 - (1 + 3) = -2$

Now, calculate the standard enthalpy of combustion ($\Delta \mathrm{H}_c^\circ$):
$\Delta \mathrm{H}_c^\circ = \Delta \mathrm{U}_c^\circ + \Delta n_g RT$
$\Delta \mathrm{H}_c^\circ = -1400 + (-2)(2.5) = -1400 - 5 = -1405 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Using Hess's Law:
$\Delta \mathrm{H}_c^\circ = 2\Delta \mathrm{H}_f^\circ(\mathrm{CO}_2) + 2\Delta \mathrm{H}_f^\circ(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}) - \Delta \mathrm{H}_f^\circ(\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_4)$
$-1405 = 2(-394) + 2(-286) - \Delta \mathrm{H}_f^\circ(\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_4)$
$-1405 = -788 - 572 - \Delta \mathrm{H}_f^\circ(\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_4)$
$-1405 = -1360 - \Delta \mathrm{H}_f^\circ(\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_4)$

$\Delta \mathrm{H}_f^\circ(\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_4) = -1360 + 1405 = 45 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

Answer: $45$

questions.question: Consider the formation of an alkaline earth metal halide $\mathrm{MX}_2(\mathrm{s})$ from its constituent elements. The enthalpy of sublimation of $\mathrm{M}(\mathrm{s})$ is $150 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$. The first and second ionization enthalpies of $\mathrm{M}(\mathrm{g})$ are $600 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$ and $1200 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$, respectively. The bond dissociation enthalpy of $\mathrm{X}_2(\mathrm{g})$ is $200 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$ and the electron gain enthalpy of $\mathrm{X}(\mathrm{g})$ is $-350 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$. The lattice dissociation enthalpy of $\mathrm{MX}_2(\mathrm{s})$ is $\qquad$ $\mathrm{kJ} \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$.
questions.solution:
The Born-Haber cycle for the formation of $\mathrm{MX}_2(\mathrm{s})$ from $\mathrm{M}(\mathrm{s})$ and $\mathrm{X}_2(\mathrm{g})$ involves the following steps:

1. Sublimation of $\mathrm{M}(\mathrm{s})$ to $\mathrm{M}(\mathrm{g})$: $\Delta \mathrm{H}_{sub} = 150 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$
2. Ionization of $\mathrm{M}(\mathrm{g})$ to $\mathrm{M}^{2+}(\mathrm{g})$: $\mathrm{IE}_1 + \mathrm{IE}_2 = 600 + 1200 = 1800 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$
3. Dissociation of one mole of $\mathrm{X}_2(\mathrm{g})$ to $2\mathrm{X}(\mathrm{g})$: $\Delta \mathrm{H}_{diss} = 200 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$ (Note: No $\dfrac{1}{2}$ factor is needed because two moles of $\mathrm{X}$ are required for $\mathrm{MX}_2$)
4. Electron gain of $2\mathrm{X}(\mathrm{g})$ to $2\mathrm{X}^{-}(\mathrm{g})$: $2 \times \Delta \mathrm{H}_{eg} = 2 \times (-350) = -700 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$
5. Formation of the lattice from gaseous ions: $\Delta \mathrm{H}_{lattice\_formation} = -\Delta \mathrm{H}_{lattice\_dissociation} = -\mathrm{U}_{diss}$

Applying Hess's Law:
$\Delta \mathrm{H}_{f} = \Delta \mathrm{H}_{sub} + (\mathrm{IE}_1 + \mathrm{IE}_2) + \Delta \mathrm{H}_{diss} + 2\Delta \mathrm{H}_{eg} - \mathrm{U}_{diss}$

Substituting the values:
$-600 = 150 + 1800 + 200 - 700 - \mathrm{U}_{diss}$

$-600 = 2150 - 700 - \mathrm{U}_{diss}$

$-600 = 1450 - \mathrm{U}_{diss}$

$\mathrm{U}_{diss} = 1450 + 600 = 2050 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$

Answer: $2050$

$C_v = \dfrac{5000}{10} = 500$ J K$^{-1}$

The total heat required is the enthalpy change for $2$ moles:

Total heat = $n \times \Delta H_{\text{vap}} = 2 \times 31.5 = 63 \text{ kJ}$

Answer: $63$

questions.question:
An ideal gas undergoes an isothermal reversible expansion at a constant temperature. The initial pressure of the gas is $5 \text{ bar}$ and its initial volume is $10 \text{ dm}^{3}$. If the gas absorbs $11.515 \text{ kJ}$ of heat from the surroundings during the process, what is the final volume of the gas?
(Given: $1 \text{ bar dm}^{3} = 100 \text{ J}$)
questions.solution:
For an isothermal process involving an ideal gas, the change in internal energy is zero ($\Delta U = 0$).

According to the First Law of Thermodynamics:
$\Delta U = q + w \Rightarrow 0 = q + w \Rightarrow w = -q$

Given that the heat absorbed $q = +11.515 \text{ kJ}$, the work done by the gas is:
$w = -11.515 \text{ kJ}$

The work done during an isothermal reversible expansion is given by:
$w = -2.303 P_{1} V_{1} \log_{10}\left(\dfrac{V_{2}}{V_{1}}\right)$

First, calculate the initial $P_{1} V_{1}$ product in Joules:
$P_{1} V_{1} = 5 \text{ bar} \times 10 \text{ dm}^{3} = 50 \text{ bar dm}^{3}$
Since $1 \text{ bar dm}^{3} = 100 \text{ J}$, we have:
$P_{1} V_{1} = 5000 \text{ J} = 5 \text{ kJ}$

Substitute the values into the work equation:
$-11.515 = -2.303 \times 5 \times \log_{10}\left(\dfrac{V_{2}}{10}\right)$
$-11.515 = -11.515 \log_{10}\left(\dfrac{V_{2}}{10}\right)$
$\log_{10}\left(\dfrac{V_{2}}{10}\right) = 1$

Taking the antilog on both sides:

If initially $1\text{ mole}$ of $A$ was taken, the percentage of $A$ converted to $B$ at equilibrium is ____.

(Given: $R = 8.3\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$, $\ln 10 = 2.3$, $\log 2 = 0.3$)
questions.solution:
For the reaction $A(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons B(\text{g})$, the standard Gibbs free energy change is given by:
$\Delta G^\circ = -2.303 RT \log K_p$

Using the given approximations:
$-3436.2 = -2.3 \times 8.3 \times 300 \times \log K_p$
$-3436.2 = -5727 \log K_p$
$\log K_p = \dfrac{3436.2}{5727} = 0.6$

Since $\log 4 = 2 \log 2 = 2(0.3) = 0.6$, we have $K_p = 4$.

Let $\alpha$ be the degree of dissociation.
Initial moles: $1$ mole of $A$, $0$ moles of $B$.
Moles at equilibrium: $(1 - \alpha)$ moles of $A$, $\alpha$ moles of $B$.

Since the number of moles does not change, the partial pressures are proportional to the number of moles.
$K_p = \dfrac{P_B}{P_A} = \dfrac{\alpha}{1 - \alpha}$

Substitute $K_p = 4$:
$4 = \dfrac{\alpha}{1 - \alpha}$
$4 - 4\alpha = \alpha$
$5\alpha = 4 \implies \alpha = 0.8$

The percentage of $A$ converted to $B$ is $0.8 \times 100 = 80$.

Answer: $80$

$\Delta_c H^\circ = \sum \Delta_f H^\circ(\text{products}) - \sum \Delta_f H^\circ(\text{reactants})$

The magnitude of the standard enthalpy of combustion is $876 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

One mole of an ideal gas is subjected to a cyclic process 1 $\rightarrow$ 2 $\rightarrow$ 3 $\rightarrow$ 1. The states of the gas are given by their Temperature (T) and Volume (V) as follows: State 1 is (600 K, 20 L), State 2 is (300 K, 20 L), and State 3 is (300 K, 10 L). The process 1 $\rightarrow$ 2 is isochoric, 2 $\rightarrow$ 3 is isothermal, and 3 $\rightarrow$ 1 is an isobaric process. The magnitude of the net work done by the gas in the cycle is _______ J.

[Given : R = 8.3 J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$, $\ln 2 = 0.7$]
questions.question:
One mole of an ideal gas is subjected to a cyclic process 1 $\rightarrow$ 2 $\rightarrow$ 3 $\rightarrow$ 1. The states of the gas are given by their Temperature (T) and Volume (V) as follows: State 1 is (600 K, 20 L), State 2 is (300 K, 20 L), and State 3 is (300 K, 10 L). The process 1 $\rightarrow$ 2 is isochoric, 2 $\rightarrow$ 3 is isothermal, and 3 $\rightarrow$ 1 is an isobaric process. The magnitude of the net work done by the gas in the cycle is _______ J.

[Given : R = 8.3 J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$, $\ln 2 = 0.7$]
questions.solution:
For the process 1 $\rightarrow$ 2 (isochoric):
Since volume is constant, the work done $W_{1 \rightarrow 2} = 0$.

For the process 2 $\rightarrow$ 3 (isothermal):
The work done is given by $W_{2 \rightarrow 3} = -nRT \ln\left(\dfrac{V_3}{V_2}\right)$
$W_{2 \rightarrow 3} = -1 \times 8.3 \times 300 \times \ln\left(\dfrac{10}{20}\right)$
$W_{2 \rightarrow 3} = -2490 \times (-\ln 2) = 2490 \times 0.7 = 1743$ J.

For the process 3 $\rightarrow$ 1 (isobaric):
The work done is given by $W_{3 \rightarrow 1} = -P(V_1 - V_3) = -nR(T_1 - T_3)$
$W_{3 \rightarrow 1} = -1 \times 8.3 \times (600 - 300) = -2490$ J.

The net work done in the cycle is:
$W_{\text{net}} = W_{1 \rightarrow 2} + W_{2 \rightarrow 3} + W_{3 \rightarrow 1}$
$W_{\text{net}} = 0 + 1743 - 2490 = -747$ J.

The magnitude of the net work done is 747 J.

Answer: $747$

The number of processes that are spontaneous at $300\text{ K}$ but become non-spontaneous at $600\text{ K}$ is _____.
questions.solution:
For a process to be spontaneous, the change in Gibbs free energy ($\Delta G$) must be negative.
$\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S$

The process is spontaneous at $300\text{ K}$ ($\Delta G_{300} < 0$) and non-spontaneous at $600\text{ K}$ ($\Delta G_{600} > 0$).
This behavior (spontaneous at low temperatures and non-spontaneous at high temperatures) occurs only when both $\Delta H < 0$ and $\Delta S < 0$. Furthermore, the crossover temperature $T_{eq} = \dfrac{\Delta H}{\Delta S}$ must lie strictly between $300\text{ K}$ and $600\text{ K}$.

Let us evaluate the crossover temperature for each process (ensuring units are matched by multiplying $\Delta H$ by $1000$):

Process 1: $T_{eq} = \dfrac{-45000}{-100} = 450\text{ K}$. Since $300 < 450 < 600$, it is spontaneous at $300\text{ K}$ and non-spontaneous at $600\text{ K}$. (Matches)

Process 2: $T_{eq} = \dfrac{-20000}{-80} = 250\text{ K}$. At $300\text{ K}$, $T > T_{eq}$, so $\Delta G > 0$. It is non-spontaneous at both $300\text{ K}$ and $600\text{ K}$. (Does not match)

Process 3: $T_{eq} = \dfrac{-60000}{-75} = 800\text{ K}$. At $600\text{ K}$, $T < T_{eq}$, so $\Delta G < 0$. It is spontaneous at both $300\text{ K}$ and $600\text{ K}$. (Does not match)

Process 4: Both $\Delta H$ and $\Delta S$ are positive. This process is non-spontaneous at low temperatures and spontaneous at high temperatures. (Does not match)

Process 5: $T_{eq} = \dfrac{-40000}{-80} = 500\text{ K}$. Since $300 < 500 < 600$, it is spontaneous at $300\text{ K}$ and non-spontaneous at $600\text{ K}$. (Matches)

Processes 1 and 5 satisfy the given conditions. The total number of such processes is $2$.

Moles of $OH^-$ from NaOH $= 150 \times 10^{-3} \times 0.5 = 0.075 \text{ mol}$

Heat released during neutralization $= 0.075 \times 56 \times 10^3 = 4200 \text{ J}$

Total volume of solution $= 150 + 150 = 300 \text{ mL}$

$= 300 \times 4.2 \times 2 = 2520 \text{ J}$

$= 4200 - 2520 = 1680 \text{ J}$

Heat capacity of the calorimeter $= \dfrac{1680}{\Delta T} = \dfrac{1680}{2} = 840 \text{ J K}^{-1}$

the standard free energy change $\Delta G^{\circ}$ at $500 \text{ K}$ and $1 \text{ atm}$ total pressure is $2324 \text{ J mol}^{-1}$. The percentage dissociation of $\mathrm{PCl}_{5}$ at equilibrium is ________.

questions.question:
For the gas-phase dissociation reaction

$\mathrm{PCl}_{5}(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{PCl}_{3}(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{Cl}_{2}(\mathrm{g})$

the standard free energy change $\Delta G^{\circ}$ at $500 \text{ K}$ and $1 \text{ atm}$ total pressure is $2324 \text{ J mol}^{-1}$. The percentage dissociation of $\mathrm{PCl}_{5}$ at equilibrium is ________.

[Given: $\ln\left(\dfrac{4}{3}\right) = 0.28$ and $\mathrm{R} = 8.3 \text{ J K}^{-1} \text{ mol}^{-1}$]
questions.solution:
The standard free energy change is related to the equilibrium constant by the equation:
$\Delta G^{\circ} = -\mathrm{RT} \ln K_{p}$

Substituting the given values:
$2324 = -8.3 \times 500 \times \ln K_{p}$
$\ln K_{p} = -\dfrac{2324}{4150} = -0.56$

Since $\ln\left(\dfrac{4}{3}\right) = 0.28$, we can write:
$-0.56 = -2 \times 0.28 = -2 \ln\left(\dfrac{4}{3}\right) = \ln\left(\dfrac{9}{16}\right)$
Thus, $K_{p} = \dfrac{9}{16}$.

For the dissociation of $\mathrm{PCl}_{5}$:
$\mathrm{PCl}_{5}(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{PCl}_{3}(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{Cl}_{2}(\mathrm{g})$
Initial moles: $1 \quad 0 \quad 0$
Equilibrium moles: $1-\alpha \quad \alpha \quad \alpha$
Total moles at equilibrium = $1 + \alpha$

The partial pressures are:
$P_{\mathrm{PCl}_{5}} = \left(\dfrac{1-\alpha}{1+\alpha}\right) P$
$P_{\mathrm{PCl}_{3}} = \left(\dfrac{\alpha}{1+\alpha}\right) P$
$P_{\mathrm{Cl}_{2}} = \left(\dfrac{\alpha}{1+\alpha}\right) P$

The equilibrium constant $K_{p}$ is:
$K_{p} = \dfrac{P_{\mathrm{PCl}_{3}} P_{\mathrm{Cl}_{2}}}{P_{\mathrm{PCl}_{5}}} = \dfrac{\alpha^{2}}{1-\alpha^{2}} P$

Given $P = 1 \text{ atm}$ and $K_{p} = \dfrac{9}{16}$:
$\dfrac{\alpha^{2}}{1-\alpha^{2}} = \dfrac{9}{16}$
$16\alpha^{2} = 9 - 9\alpha^{2}$
$25\alpha^{2} = 9$
$\alpha^{2} = \dfrac{9}{25} \implies \alpha = \dfrac{3}{5} = 0.6$

The percentage dissociation is $0.6 \times 100 = 60\%$.

Answer: $60$

The molar mass of $\mathrm{N}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4}$ is $2(14) + 4(16) = 92 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$.
The vapor density of pure $\mathrm{N}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4}$ ($D$) is $\dfrac{92}{2} = 46$.

Here, $1$ mole of $\mathrm{N}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4}$ gives $2$ moles of $\mathrm{NO}_{2}$, so $n = 2$.

Here, $1$ mole of $\mathrm{N}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4}$ gives $2$ moles of $\mathrm{NO}_{2}$, so $n = 2$.

Initial moles: $1 \quad 0$

Answer: $1726$

Two moles of an ideal gas expand isothermally from an initial pressure of $10 \text{ bar}$ to a final pressure of $1 \text{ bar}$ at $300 \text{ K}$. What is the magnitude of the difference between the work done if the process is carried out reversibly and the work done if it is carried out irreversibly against a constant external pressure of $1 \text{ bar}$?

questions.question:

What is the magnitude of the difference between the work done if the process is carried out reversibly and the work done if it is carried out irreversibly against a constant external pressure of $1 \text{ bar}$?
(Given: $R = 8.3 \text{ J K}^{-1} \text{ mol}^{-1}$, $\ln 10 = 2.3$)
questions.solution:
First, calculate the work done during the reversible isothermal expansion ($w_{rev}$):
$w_{rev} = -nRT \ln\left(\dfrac{P_{1}}{P_{2}}\right)$
$w_{rev} = -2 \times 8.3 \times 300 \times \ln\left(\dfrac{10}{1}\right)$
$w_{rev} = -4980 \times 2.3 = -11454 \text{ J}$

Next, calculate the work done during the irreversible isothermal expansion ($w_{irr}$) against a constant external pressure $P_{ext} = 1 \text{ bar}$:
$w_{irr} = -P_{ext} (V_{2} - V_{1})$
Using the ideal gas law $V = \dfrac{nRT}{P}$, we can substitute the volumes:
$w_{irr} = -P_{ext} \left(\dfrac{nRT}{P_{2}} - \dfrac{nRT}{P_{1}}\right)$
Since the external pressure equals the final pressure ($P_{ext} = P_{2}$):
$w_{irr} = -nRT \left(1 - \dfrac{P_{2}}{P_{1}}\right)$
$w_{irr} = -4980 \left(1 - \dfrac{1}{10}\right) = -4980 \times 0.9 = -4482 \text{ J}$

Finally, find the magnitude of the difference between the two work values:
$|w_{rev} - w_{irr}| = |-11454 - (-4482)|$
$|w_{rev} - w_{irr}| = |-11454 + 4482| = |-6972| = 6972 \text{ J}$

Answer: $6972 \text{ J}$

questions.q: For a hypothetical gas-phase reaction, the natural logarithm of the equilibrium constant ($\ln K$) is found to be $40$ at $T = 300 \text{ K}$ and $10$ at $T = 400 \text{ K}$. Assuming that the standard enthalpy change ($\Delta H^{\circ}$) and standard entropy change ($\Delta S^{\circ}$) for the reaction are independent of temperature, at what temperature will the standard Gibbs free energy change ($\Delta G^{\circ}$) be zero?
questions.question: For a hypothetical gas-phase reaction, the natural logarithm of the equilibrium constant ($\ln K$) is found to be $40$ at $T = 300 \text{ K}$ and $10$ at $T = 400 \text{ K}$. Assuming that the standard enthalpy change ($\Delta H^{\circ}$) and standard entropy change ($\Delta S^{\circ}$) for the reaction are independent of temperature, at what temperature will the standard Gibbs free energy change ($\Delta G^{\circ}$) be zero?
questions.solution:
The relationship between the equilibrium constant and temperature is given by the van 't Hoff equation:
$\ln K = -\dfrac{\Delta H^{\circ}}{RT} + \dfrac{\Delta S^{\circ}}{R}$

This indicates that $\ln K$ is a linear function of $1/T$. Let $y = \ln K$ and $x = 1/T$. We are given two points: $(x_1, y_1) = (1/300, 40)$ and $(x_2, y_2) = (1/400, 10)$.

First, we find the slope $m$ of this line:
$m = \dfrac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1} = \dfrac{10 - 40}{\dfrac{1}{400} - \dfrac{1}{300}} = \dfrac{-30}{\dfrac{3 - 4}{1200}} = \dfrac{-30}{-\dfrac{1}{1200}} = 36000$

Using the point-slope form $y - y_2 = m(x - x_2)$, the equation of the line is:
$\ln K - 10 = 36000 \left(\dfrac{1}{T} - \dfrac{1}{400}\right)$

We need to find the temperature at which $\Delta G^{\circ} = 0$. Since $\Delta G^{\circ} = -RT \ln K$, $\Delta G^{\circ} = 0$ corresponds to $\ln K = 0$.

Substituting $\ln K = 0$ into the equation:
$0 - 10 = 36000 \left(\dfrac{1}{T} - \dfrac{1}{400}\right)$
$\dfrac{-10}{36000} = \dfrac{1}{T} - \dfrac{1}{400}$
$-\dfrac{1}{3600} = \dfrac{1}{T} - \dfrac{1}{400}$
$\dfrac{1}{T} = \dfrac{1}{400} - \dfrac{1}{3600} = \dfrac{9 - 1}{3600} = \dfrac{8}{3600} = \dfrac{1}{450}$

Therefore, $T = 450 \text{ K}$.

Answer: $450 \text{ K}$

An ideal gas undergoes a cyclic process 1 $\rightarrow$ 2 $\rightarrow$ 3 $\rightarrow$ 1 described as follows:
Step 1 $\rightarrow$ 2: Isobaric expansion from volume $V$ to $2V$.
Step 2 $\rightarrow$ 3: Isochoric cooling until the pressure is halved.
Step 3 $\rightarrow$ 1: Isothermal compression at 400 K back to the initial state 1.

If the magnitude of the net work done in the entire cycle is 2988 J, the number of moles of the gas is _______.

[Given: R = 8.3 J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$, $\ln 2 = 0.7$]
questions.question:
An ideal gas undergoes a cyclic process 1 $\rightarrow$ 2 $\rightarrow$ 3 $\rightarrow$ 1 described as follows:
Step 1 $\rightarrow$ 2: Isobaric expansion from volume $V$ to $2V$.
Step 2 $\rightarrow$ 3: Isochoric cooling until the pressure is halved.
Step 3 $\rightarrow$ 1: Isothermal compression at 400 K back to the initial state 1.

If the magnitude of the net work done in the entire cycle is 2988 J, the number of moles of the gas is _______.

[Given: R = 8.3 J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$, $\ln 2 = 0.7$]
questions.solution:
Let the number of moles of the gas be $n$.

In state 1, the gas is at temperature $T_1 = 400$ K (since step 3 $\rightarrow$ 1 is isothermal at 400 K and returns to state 1).

Step 1 $\rightarrow$ 2 is an isobaric expansion from $V$ to $2V$.
Since $V \propto T$ at constant pressure, $T_2 = 2T_1 = 800$ K.
Work done $W_{1 \rightarrow 2} = -nR(T_2 - T_1) = -n \times 8.3 \times (800 - 400) = -3320n$ J.

Step 2 $\rightarrow$ 3 is an isochoric process.
Since volume is constant, work done $W_{2 \rightarrow 3} = 0$.

Step 3 $\rightarrow$ 1 is an isothermal compression at 400 K from $2V$ back to $V$.
Work done $W_{3 \rightarrow 1} = -nRT_1 \ln\left(\dfrac{V_1}{V_3}\right)$
$W_{3 \rightarrow 1} = -n \times 8.3 \times 400 \times \ln\left(\dfrac{V}{2V}\right)$
$W_{3 \rightarrow 1} = -3320n \times (-\ln 2) = 3320n \times 0.7 = 2324n$ J.

The net work done in the cycle is:
$W_{\text{net}} = W_{1 \rightarrow 2} + W_{2 \rightarrow 3} + W_{3 \rightarrow 1}$
$W_{\text{net}} = -3320n + 0 + 2324n = -996n$ J.

The magnitude of the net work done is $996n$ J.
Given that the magnitude is 2988 J:
$996n = 2988$
$n = 3$

The number of moles of the gas is 3.

Answer: $3$

Let $m_1$, $m_2$, and $m_3$ be the slopes of the plots of standard Gibbs free energy change ($\Delta G^{\circ}$) versus temperature ($T$) for reactions (i), (ii), and (iii) respectively. Which of the following relations correctly orders these slopes?

Consider the following three gas-phase reactions and assume that their standard enthalpy ($\Delta H^{\circ}$) and standard entropy ($\Delta S^{\circ}$) changes are independent of temperature:

(i) $\mathrm{N_2(g) + O_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2NO(g)}$
(ii) $\mathrm{N_2(g) + 3H_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2NH_3(g)}$
(iii) $\mathrm{N_2O_4(g) \rightleftharpoons 2NO_2(g)}$

Let $m_1$, $m_2$, and $m_3$ be the slopes of the plots of standard Gibbs free energy change ($\Delta G^{\circ}$) versus temperature ($T$) for reactions (i), (ii), and (iii) respectively. Which of the following relations correctly orders these slopes?
questions.solution:
The standard Gibbs free energy change is given by the equation:
$\Delta G^{\circ} = \Delta H^{\circ} - T\Delta S^{\circ}$

When $\Delta G^{\circ}$ is plotted against $T$, the equation represents a straight line ($y = c + mx$) where the slope $m = -\Delta S^{\circ}$.

The sign of $\Delta S^{\circ}$ can be predicted from the change in the number of gaseous moles ($\Delta n_g$):
For reaction (i): $\Delta n_g = 2 - (1 + 1) = 0$. Thus, $\Delta S^{\circ} \approx 0$, which means $m_1 \approx 0$.
For reaction (ii): $\Delta n_g = 2 - (1 + 3) = -2$. The number of gaseous moles decreases, so $\Delta S^{\circ} < 0$. Therefore, the slope $m_2 = -\Delta S^{\circ} > 0$.
For reaction (iii): $\Delta n_g = 2 - 1 = +1$. The number of gaseous moles increases, so $\Delta S^{\circ} > 0$. Therefore, the slope $m_3 = -\Delta S^{\circ} < 0$.

Comparing the slopes, we have $m_3 < 0$, $m_1 \approx 0$, and $m_2 > 0$.
Hence, the correct order is $m_3 < m_1 < m_2$.

Answer: $m_3 < m_1 < m_2$

$\Delta U = Q + W \Rightarrow W = -Q$

Since heat is released by the gas, $Q = -200 \text{ L atm}$.
Therefore, work done on the gas is $W = +200 \text{ L atm}$.

For compression against a constant external pressure, the work done is given by:
$W = -P_{\text{ext}}(V_f - V_i)$

Substituting the given values:
$200 = -4(10 - V_i)$
$-50 = 10 - V_i$
$V_i = 60 \text{ L}$

Answer: $60$

questions.q: The standard enthalpy of formation of ethane ($\mathrm{C_2H_6(g)}$) is $-84 \mathrm{~kJ \ mol^{-1}}$. The enthalpy of sublimation of graphite is $716 \mathrm{~kJ \ mol^{-1}}$ and the bond dissociation enthalpy of $\mathrm{H_2(g)}$ is $436 \mathrm{~kJ \ mol^{-1}}$. If the average $\mathrm{C-H}$ bond enthalpy is $412 \mathrm{~kJ \ mol^{-1}}$, the $\mathrm{C-C}$ bond enthalpy in ethane is __________ $\mathrm{kJ \ mol^{-1}}$.
questions.question: The standard enthalpy of formation of ethane ($\mathrm{C_2H_6(g)}$) is $-84 \mathrm{~kJ \ mol^{-1}}$. The enthalpy of sublimation of graphite is $716 \mathrm{~kJ \ mol^{-1}}$ and the bond dissociation enthalpy of $\mathrm{H_2(g)}$ is $436 \mathrm{~kJ \ mol^{-1}}$. If the average $\mathrm{C-H}$ bond enthalpy is $412 \mathrm{~kJ \ mol^{-1}}$, the $\mathrm{C-C}$ bond enthalpy in ethane is __________ $\mathrm{kJ \ mol^{-1}}$.
questions.solution:
The enthalpy of atomization of ethane ($\mathrm{C_2H_6(g)}$) corresponds to the reaction:
$\mathrm{C_2H_6(g)} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{C(g)} + 6\mathrm{H(g)}$

The standard enthalpy of formation of gaseous carbon atoms is equal to the enthalpy of sublimation of graphite:
$\Delta_{\mathrm{f}}\mathrm{H}^{\ominus}(\mathrm{C(g)}) = 716 \mathrm{~kJ \ mol^{-1}}$

The standard enthalpy of formation of gaseous hydrogen atoms is half the bond dissociation enthalpy of $\mathrm{H_2(g)}$:
$\Delta_{\mathrm{f}}\mathrm{H}^{\ominus}(\mathrm{H(g)}) = \dfrac{436}{2} = 218 \mathrm{~kJ \ mol^{-1}}$

Using Hess's Law, the enthalpy of atomization of ethane is:
$\Delta_{\mathrm{atom}}\mathrm{H} = 2\Delta_{\mathrm{f}}\mathrm{H}^{\ominus}(\mathrm{C(g)}) + 6\Delta_{\mathrm{f}}\mathrm{H}^{\ominus}(\mathrm{H(g)}) - \Delta_{\mathrm{f}}\mathrm{H}^{\ominus}(\mathrm{C_2H_6(g)})$
$\Delta_{\mathrm{atom}}\mathrm{H} = 2(716) + 6(218) - (-84)$
$\Delta_{\mathrm{atom}}\mathrm{H} = 1432 + 1308 + 84 = 2824 \mathrm{~kJ \ mol^{-1}}$

The total atomization energy is also the sum of all bond enthalpies in the molecule. Ethane has one $\mathrm{C-C}$ bond and six $\mathrm{C-H}$ bonds:
$\Delta_{\mathrm{atom}}\mathrm{H} = \mathrm{BE(C-C)} + 6 \times \mathrm{BE(C-H)}$
$2824 = \mathrm{BE(C-C)} + 6(412)$
$2824 = \mathrm{BE(C-C)} + 2472$

$\mathrm{BE(C-C)} = 2824 - 2472 = 352 \mathrm{~kJ \ mol^{-1}}$

Answer: $352$

$\Delta_{\mathrm{atom}}\mathrm{H} = 2(716) + 6(218) - (-84)$

$2824 = \mathrm{BE(C-C)} + 6(412)$
$2824 = \mathrm{BE(C-C)} + 2472$

Answer: $352$

$\Delta H_{\text{vap}} = -235 - (-280) = 45 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1} = 45000 \text{ J mol}^{-1}$

$\Delta S_{\text{vap}} = S^{\circ}(\text{g}) - S^{\circ}(\text{l})$
$\Delta S_{\text{vap}} = 210 - 120 = 90 \text{ J K}^{-1} \text{ mol}^{-1}$

$\Delta G = \Delta H_{\text{vap}} - T_{b} \Delta S_{\text{vap}} = 0$

$T_{b} = \dfrac{\Delta H_{\text{vap}}}{\Delta S_{\text{vap}}}$

$T_{b} = \dfrac{45000}{90} = 500 \text{ K}$

Answer: $500$

$n = \dfrac{200}{400} = 0.5 \text{ mol}$.

Mass of graphite burnt $= n \times \text{Molar mass of carbon} = 0.5 \times 12 = 6 \text{ g}$.

The observed vapour density of the equilibrium mixture at a total pressure of $1.2\text{ atm}$ is $69.5$. The standard Gibbs free energy change ($\Delta G^\circ$) for the reaction at $300\text{ K}$ is ____ $\text{J mol}^{-1}$ (nearest integer).

(Given: Molar mass of $\text{PCl}_5 = 208.5\text{ g mol}^{-1}$, $R = 8.3\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$, $\ln 10 = 2.3$, $\log 2 = 0.3$)
questions.question:
The decomposition of $\text{PCl}_5(\text{g})$ into $\text{PCl}_3(\text{g})$ and $\text{Cl}_2(\text{g})$ is carried out at $300\text{ K}$. The observed vapour density of the equilibrium mixture at a total pressure of $1.2\text{ atm}$ is $69.5$. The standard Gibbs free energy change ($\Delta G^\circ$) for the reaction at $300\text{ K}$ is ____ $\text{J mol}^{-1}$ (nearest integer).

(Given: Molar mass of $\text{PCl}_5 = 208.5\text{ g mol}^{-1}$, $R = 8.3\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$, $\ln 10 = 2.3$, $\log 2 = 0.3$)
questions.solution:
Theoretical vapour density of $\text{PCl}_5$ ($D$) = $\dfrac{\text{Molar mass}}{2} = \dfrac{208.5}{2} = 104.25$

Degree of dissociation ($\alpha$) is given by:
$\alpha = \dfrac{D - d}{(n - 1)d}$
Here, $n = 2$ (since $1$ mole of $\text{PCl}_5$ gives $2$ moles of products).
$\alpha = \dfrac{104.25 - 69.5}{(2 - 1) \times 69.5} = \dfrac{34.75}{69.5} = 0.5$

For the reaction $\text{PCl}_5(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons \text{PCl}_3(\text{g}) + \text{Cl}_2(\text{g})$:
Total moles at equilibrium = $1 + \alpha$
$K_p = \dfrac{\alpha^2}{1 - \alpha^2} \times P$
$K_p = \dfrac{(0.5)^2}{1 - (0.5)^2} \times 1.2 = \dfrac{0.25}{0.75} \times 1.2 = \dfrac{1}{3} \times 1.2 = 0.4$

Standard Gibbs free energy change:
$\Delta G^\circ = -2.303 RT \log K_p$
Using the given approximations:
$\Delta G^\circ = -2.3 \times 8.3 \times 300 \times \log(0.4)$
$\log(0.4) = \log\left(\dfrac{4}{10}\right) = 2\log 2 - 1 = 2(0.3) - 1 = -0.4$

$\Delta G^\circ = -5727 \times (-0.4) = 2290.8\text{ J mol}^{-1}$

Rounding off to the nearest integer, we get $2291$.

Answer: $2291$

questions.solution:
The relationship between change in Gibbs free energy, enthalpy, and entropy at a constant temperature is given by:
$\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S$

Rearranging for $\Delta S$:
$\Delta S = \dfrac{\Delta H - \Delta G}{T}$

We are looking for processes where $\Delta S < -20\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$.
Substituting $T = 300\text{ K}$ and converting the condition into $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$:
$\dfrac{\Delta H - \Delta G}{300} < -20$
$\Delta H - \Delta G < -6000\text{ J mol}^{-1}$
$\Delta G - \Delta H > 6\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Let us check this condition for each process:
Process A: $\Delta G - \Delta H = -11 - (-20) = 9\text{ kJ mol}^{-1} > 6$ (Satisfies)
Process B: $\Delta G - \Delta H = -47 - (-50) = 3\text{ kJ mol}^{-1} \ngtr 6$ (Does not satisfy)
Process C: $\Delta G - \Delta H = 42 - 30 = 12\text{ kJ mol}^{-1} > 6$ (Satisfies)
Process D: $\Delta G - \Delta H = 10 - 10 = 0\text{ kJ mol}^{-1} \ngtr 6$ (Does not satisfy)
Process E: $\Delta G - \Delta H = -1 - (-10) = 9\text{ kJ mol}^{-1} > 6$ (Satisfies)

Processes A, C, and E satisfy the condition. Therefore, the number of such processes is $3$.

Answer: $3$

A gaseous mixture of methane ($\text{CH}_4$) and propane ($\text{C}_3\text{H}_8$) has a total volume of $44.8 \text{ L}$ at $273 \text{ K}$ and $1 \text{ atm}$. On complete combustion, the mixture evolves $3780 \text{ kJ}$ of heat. The volume of $\text{CO}_2$ gas produced at $273 \text{ K}$ and $1 \text{ atm}$ is ________ $\text{L}$.

Given:
$\Delta H_c (\text{CH}_4) = -900 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Molar volume of an ideal gas at $273 \text{ K}$ and $1 \text{ atm}$ is $22.4 \text{ L mol}^{-1}$.
questions.solution:
Let the total moles of the mixture be $n$.
$n = \dfrac{44.8}{22.4} = 2 \text{ moles}$

Let the moles of $\text{CH}_4$ be $x$ and the moles of $\text{C}_3\text{H}_8$ be $(2 - x)$.
The total heat evolved is the sum of the heat evolved by the combustion of each gas:
$900x + 2220(2 - x) = 3780$
$900x + 4440 - 2220x = 3780$
$1320x = 660 \Rightarrow x = 0.5 \text{ mol}$

Moles of $\text{CH}_4 = 0.5 \text{ mol}$
Moles of $\text{C}_3\text{H}_8 = 1.5 \text{ mol}$

The combustion reactions are:
$\text{CH}_4 + 2\text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{CO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$
$\text{C}_3\text{H}_8 + 5\text{O}_2 \rightarrow 3\text{CO}_2 + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$

Total moles of $\text{CO}_2$ produced = $1 \times n_{\text{CH}_4} + 3 \times n_{\text{C}_3\text{H}_8}$
$n_{\text{CO}_2} = 1(0.5) + 3(1.5) = 5 \text{ moles}$

Volume of $\text{CO}_2$ produced at $273 \text{ K}$ and $1 \text{ atm}$ = $5 \times 22.4 = 112 \text{ L}$.

Answer: $112$

questions.q: An ideal gas is enclosed in a cylinder fitted with a frictionless piston and perfectly heat-conducting walls. The cylinder is immersed in a large constant-temperature water bath. The gas is then slowly compressed by gradually adding weights to the piston. Which of the following sets of thermodynamic parameters correctly describes this process?
questions.question: An ideal gas is enclosed in a cylinder fitted with a frictionless piston and perfectly heat-conducting walls. The cylinder is immersed in a large constant-temperature water bath. The gas is then slowly compressed by gradually adding weights to the piston. Which of the following sets of thermodynamic parameters correctly describes this process?
questions.solution:
The cylinder has perfectly heat-conducting walls and is placed in a constant-temperature bath, and the process is slow. This ensures the process is isothermal. For an ideal gas undergoing an isothermal process, the change in internal energy is zero ($\Delta \mathrm{U} = 0$).

The gas is being compressed by external weights, which means work is done on the system. According to IUPAC sign convention, work done on the system is positive ($\mathrm{w} \gt 0$).

Applying the First Law of Thermodynamics:
$\Delta \mathrm{U} = \mathrm{q} + \mathrm{w}$
$0 = \mathrm{q} + \mathrm{w}$
$\mathrm{q} = -\mathrm{w}$
Since $\mathrm{w} \gt 0$, it follows that $\mathrm{q} \lt 0$ (heat flows out of the system into the bath).

Answer: $\Delta \mathrm{U} = 0, \mathrm{q} \lt 0, \mathrm{w} \gt 0$

The magnitude of the standard enthalpy change for the oxidation of ammonia,

At $298\text{ K}$, the standard enthalpies of formation for $\text{NH}_3(\text{g})$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l})$ are $-46\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ and $-286\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, respectively. The enthalpies of the following reactions at $298\text{ K}$ are given:

$\text{N}_2(\text{g}) + 2\text{O}_2(\text{g}) \rightarrow 2\text{NO}_2(\text{g})$, $\Delta\text{H}^\circ = +66\text{ kJ}$
$\text{N}_2(\text{g}) + \text{O}_2(\text{g}) \rightarrow 2\text{NO}(\text{g})$, $\Delta\text{H}^\circ = +180\text{ kJ}$

The magnitude of the standard enthalpy change for the oxidation of ammonia,
$4\text{NH}_3(\text{g}) + 7\text{O}_2(\text{g}) \rightarrow 4\text{NO}_2(\text{g}) + 6\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l})$
is ________ $\text{kJ}$. (Nearest integer)
questions.solution:
The standard enthalpy of reaction is given by:
$\Delta\text{H}^\circ_{\text{rxn}} = \sum \Delta\text{H}^\circ_{\text{f}}(\text{products}) - \sum \Delta\text{H}^\circ_{\text{f}}(\text{reactants})$

From the given data:
$\Delta\text{H}^\circ_{\text{f}}(\text{NH}_3, \text{g}) = -46\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
$\Delta\text{H}^\circ_{\text{f}}(\text{H}_2\text{O}, \text{l}) = -286\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

For $\text{NO}_2(\text{g})$, the standard formation reaction is $\dfrac{1}{2}\text{N}_2(\text{g}) + \text{O}_2(\text{g}) \rightarrow \text{NO}_2(\text{g})$.
Given $\text{N}_2(\text{g}) + 2\text{O}_2(\text{g}) \rightarrow 2\text{NO}_2(\text{g})$ with $\Delta\text{H}^\circ = 66\text{ kJ}$, we have:
$\Delta\text{H}^\circ_{\text{f}}(\text{NO}_2, \text{g}) = \dfrac{66}{2} = 33\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.
(The reaction for $\text{NO}$ is extra information and not needed).

Now, substituting these values into the formula for the given reaction:
$\Delta\text{H}^\circ_{\text{rxn}} = [4 \times \Delta\text{H}^\circ_{\text{f}}(\text{NO}_2) + 6 \times \Delta\text{H}^\circ_{\text{f}}(\text{H}_2\text{O})] - [4 \times \Delta\text{H}^\circ_{\text{f}}(\text{NH}_3) + 7 \times \Delta\text{H}^\circ_{\text{f}}(\text{O}_2)]$
$\Delta\text{H}^\circ_{\text{rxn}} = [4 \times 33 + 6 \times (-286)] - [4 \times (-46) + 7 \times 0]$
$\Delta\text{H}^\circ_{\text{rxn}} = [132 - 1716] - [-184]$
$\Delta\text{H}^\circ_{\text{rxn}} = -1584 + 184 = -1400\text{ kJ}$

The magnitude of the enthalpy change is $1400\text{ kJ}$.

Answer: $1400$

questions.q:
$12 \text{ g}$ of a gaseous mixture of ethene ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$) and methane ($\text{CH}_4$) produces $35.2 \text{ g}$ of $\text{CO}_2$ gas on complete combustion. If this mixture is combusted in a rigid bomb calorimeter at $300 \text{ K}$, the magnitude of heat evolved is ________ $\text{kJ}$. (Nearest integer)

Given:
$\Delta H_c^\circ (\text{C}_2\text{H}_4, \text{g}) = -1400 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
$\Delta H_c^\circ (\text{CH}_4, \text{g}) = -900 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

questions.question:
$12 \text{ g}$ of a gaseous mixture of ethene ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$) and methane ($\text{CH}_4$) produces $35.2 \text{ g}$ of $\text{CO}_2$ gas on complete combustion. If this mixture is combusted in a rigid bomb calorimeter at $300 \text{ K}$, the magnitude of heat evolved is ________ $\text{kJ}$. (Nearest integer)

Given:

$\Delta H_c^\circ (\text{CH}_4, \text{g}) = -900 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
$R = \dfrac{25}{3} \text{ J K}^{-1} \text{mol}^{-1}$
questions.solution:
Let the moles of $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$ be $x$ and $\text{CH}_4$ be $y$.
Mass of the mixture:
$28x + 16y = 12$

Moles of $\text{CO}_2$ produced = $\dfrac{35.2}{44} = 0.8 \text{ mol}$
From the stoichiometry of combustion, $1 \text{ mole}$ of $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$ gives $2 \text{ moles}$ of $\text{CO}_2$, and $1 \text{ mole}$ of $\text{CH}_4$ gives $1 \text{ mole}$ of $\text{CO}_2$.
$2x + y = 0.8 \Rightarrow y = 0.8 - 2x$

Substituting $y$ into the mass equation:
$28x + 16(0.8 - 2x) = 12$
$28x + 12.8 - 32x = 12$
$4x = 0.8 \Rightarrow x = 0.2 \text{ mol}$
$y = 0.8 - 2(0.2) = 0.4 \text{ mol}$

Total enthalpy of combustion ($\Delta H$):
$\Delta H = 0.2(-1400) + 0.4(-900) = -280 - 360 = -640 \text{ kJ}$

The combustion reactions are:
$\text{C}_2\text{H}_4(\text{g}) + 3\text{O}_2(\text{g}) \rightarrow 2\text{CO}_2(\text{g}) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l})$, $\Delta n_g = 2 - (1 + 3) = -2$
$\text{CH}_4(\text{g}) + 2\text{O}_2(\text{g}) \rightarrow \text{CO}_2(\text{g}) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l})$, $\Delta n_g = 1 - (1 + 2) = -2$

Total change in gaseous moles ($\Delta n_g$):
$\Delta n_g = 0.2(-2) + 0.4(-2) = -1.2 \text{ mol}$

Heat evolved in a bomb calorimeter is the change in internal energy ($-\Delta U$).
Using the First Law of Thermodynamics:
$\Delta H = \Delta U + \Delta n_g RT$
$\Delta U = \Delta H - \Delta n_g RT$
$\Delta U = -640 - \left(-1.2 \times \dfrac{25}{3} \times 300 \times 10^{-3}\right)$
$\Delta U = -640 - (-3) = -637 \text{ kJ}$

The magnitude of heat evolved is $637 \text{ kJ}$.

Answer: $637$

Heat evolved in a bomb calorimeter is the change in internal energy ($-\Delta U$).
Using the First Law of Thermodynamics:
$\Delta H = \Delta U + \Delta n_g RT$
$\Delta U = \Delta H - \Delta n_g RT$
$\Delta U = -640 - \left(-1.2 \times \dfrac{25}{3} \times 300 \times 10^{-3}\right)$
$\Delta U = -640 - (-3) = -637 \text{ kJ}$

The magnitude of heat evolved is $637 \text{ kJ}$.

Answer: $637$

When $1.4\text{ g}$ of ethylene ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$) undergoes combustion in a bomb calorimeter at $300\text{ K}$, the temperature of the calorimeter system rises by $5\text{ K}$. The heat capacity of the calorimeter system is $14.1\text{ kJ K}^{-1}$.

Given the standard enthalpies of formation of $\text{CO}_2(\text{g})$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l})$ are $-393.5\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ and $-286\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ respectively.

The standard enthalpy of formation of ethylene is ________ $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. (Nearest integer)

[Given: $R = 8.3\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$, molar mass of $\text{C}$ and $\text{H}$ are $12$ and $1\text{ g mol}^{-1}$ respectively. Assume ideal gas behaviour.]
questions.question:
When $1.4\text{ g}$ of ethylene ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$) undergoes combustion in a bomb calorimeter at $300\text{ K}$, the temperature of the calorimeter system rises by $5\text{ K}$. The heat capacity of the calorimeter system is $14.1\text{ kJ K}^{-1}$.

Given the standard enthalpies of formation of $\text{CO}_2(\text{g})$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l})$ are $-393.5\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ and $-286\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ respectively.

The standard enthalpy of formation of ethylene is ________ $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. (Nearest integer)

[Given: $R = 8.3\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$, molar mass of $\text{C}$ and $\text{H}$ are $12$ and $1\text{ g mol}^{-1}$ respectively. Assume ideal gas behaviour.]
questions.solution:
The heat released in the bomb calorimeter at constant volume is:
$q_v = C_v \times \Delta T = 14.1 \times 5 = 70.5\text{ kJ}$

Molar mass of $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4 = 2(12) + 4(1) = 28\text{ g mol}^{-1}$
Moles of ethylene burnt $= \dfrac{1.4}{28} = 0.05\text{ mol}$

Molar internal energy of combustion ($\Delta U_{comb}$) is:
$\Delta U_{comb} = -\dfrac{70.5}{0.05} = -1410\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

The combustion reaction of ethylene is:
$\text{C}_2\text{H}_4(\text{g}) + 3\text{O}_2(\text{g}) \rightarrow 2\text{CO}_2(\text{g}) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l})$

Change in gaseous moles:
$\Delta n_g = 2 - (1 + 3) = -2$

Enthalpy of combustion ($\Delta H_{comb}$) is:
$\Delta H_{comb} = \Delta U_{comb} + \Delta n_g RT$
$\Delta H_{comb} = -1410 + \dfrac{-2 \times 8.3 \times 300}{1000}$
$\Delta H_{comb} = -1410 - 4.98 = -1414.98\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Using Hess's Law for the combustion reaction:
$\Delta H_{comb} = 2\Delta H_f(\text{CO}_2) + 2\Delta H_f(\text{H}_2\text{O}) - \Delta H_f(\text{C}_2\text{H}_4)$
$-1414.98 = 2(-393.5) + 2(-286) - \Delta H_f(\text{C}_2\text{H}_4)$
$-1414.98 = -787 - 572 - \Delta H_f(\text{C}_2\text{H}_4)$
$-1414.98 = -1359 - \Delta H_f(\text{C}_2\text{H}_4)$

Solving for the enthalpy of formation of ethylene:
$\Delta H_f(\text{C}_2\text{H}_4) = -1359 + 1414.98 = 55.98\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Rounding to the nearest integer, we get $56$.

Answer: $56$
